desc:
You may choose any elements of nums as long as you never choose three elements with consecutive indices (i, i + 1 and i + 2 must not all be chosen). Two chosen neighbours are fine.

Return the largest possible sum of the chosen elements. Choosing nothing is allowed.

For example, in [3, 4, 5, 1] the choice 4 + 5 + 1 is illegal (indices 1, 2, 3 are consecutive), but 3 + 5 + 1 = 9 and 4 + 5 = 9 are fine, and 9 is the best possible.
hints: Since all values are non-negative, you want to choose as many elements as the rule allows. The rule only cares about how many chosen elements in a row you just made.
Track the length of the current streak of chosen elements: 0, 1 or 2. A streak of 2 forces you to skip the next element.
Keep three values: best sum ending with a skip, with a streak of 1 and with a streak of 2. Choosing x moves streak s to s + 1 (and adds x); skipping resets the streak to 0.
editorial: Let s0, s1, s2 be the best sums over the prefix processed so far where the current run of chosen elements at the end has length 0, 1 or 2. Reading element x: new s0 = max(s0, s1, s2) (skip it), new s1 = s0 + x and new s2 = s1 + x. A run of length 2 cannot be extended, which is exactly the forbidden triple.

Start with s0 = 0 and the other two impossible. The answer is the maximum of the three at the end. Alternatively the problem can be seen as removing the cheapest set of elements so that every window of three has a removed one, but the three-state DP is simpler. Time O(n), space O(1).
